scope: Exact OSM ID overlap between the current published atlas and historical extraction. No current geometry changes made. Also audited all other destroyed-lifecycle objects; all 56 are in the same Kumamoto flood-damaged corridors and lack closure dates.
decision_policy: An infrastructure destroyed/disused/historic tag alone is not proof of permanent closure. For exact ID conflicts, omit the historical copy until source evidence supports a permanently closed alignment or a fully documented replacement of the current feature.

limits: Current dataset includes geographically mapped corridors that can be under disaster suspension; keeping current representation does not assert trains presently operate on every section.
Operator reopening may involve rebuilt or relocated geometry, so raw historical and current source IDs are not definitive coordinate provenance.
This report does not audit historical OSM objects absent from the current atlas.

set.end_date_type: formal relocation/replacement date; not the date of the last train before flood suspension
set.certainty: former location confirmed by operator; replacement present in current OSM snapshot

current_station_patch.indexing_note: Filter the obsolete object from current search and station point collections, then rebuild dense indices as usual; do not delete its historical feature. Do not remove the operating Yunomae Line geometry.
